---
title: "Where they overlap"
toc: false
subtitle: "Research question 1: where do high anemia, open defecation, and malaria coincide?"
---

```{python}
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
from _common import hexes, regions, VAR, PROFILE_COLORS
hx = pd.DataFrame(hexes().drop(columns="geometry"))
rg = regions(0.03)
rg = rg[rg.n_clusters.notna()].copy()
med = {c: rg[c].median() for c in ["anemia_pct", "od_pct", "pfpr"]}
rg["n_high"] = sum((rg[c] > med[c]).astype(int) for c in med)
rg["high_label"] = rg.n_high.map({0: "None of the three", 1: "One", 2: "Two", 3: "All three"})
```

## How many of the three are high, region by region?

For every region (admin-1: a province or state) I check whether anemia, open defecation, and malaria are **above the median region** in this sample. Dark red means all three are high at once.

::: {.howto}
**Click a country bar** on the right to highlight its regions on the map. Shift-click to pick several. Double-click to reset.
:::

```{python}
high_scale = alt.Scale(domain=["None of the three", "One", "Two", "All three"],
                       range=["#e8eef2", "#f6c4a6", "#e2654a", "#8e0f14"])
pick = alt.selection_point(fields=["country"], on="click")
mapc = alt.Chart(rg).mark_geoshape(stroke="white", strokeWidth=0.4).encode(
    color=alt.Color("high_label:N", scale=high_scale, title="Above-median measures",
                    sort=["None of the three", "One", "Two", "All three"]),
    opacity=alt.condition(pick, alt.value(1), alt.value(0.15)),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("region:N", title="Region"), alt.Tooltip("country:N"),
             alt.Tooltip("anemia_pct:Q", title="Anemia %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("od_pct:Q", title="No toilet %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("pfpr:Q", title="Malaria %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("n_clusters:Q", title="DHS clusters")]
).project("equalEarth").properties(width=520, height=520)

bars = alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame(rg.drop(columns="geometry"))).mark_bar().encode(
    y=alt.Y("country:N", sort="-x", title=None),
    x=alt.X("count():Q", title="Number of regions", stack="normalize", axis=alt.Axis(format="%")),
    color=alt.Color("high_label:N", scale=high_scale, sort=["None of the three", "One", "Two", "All three"],
                    legend=None),
    order=alt.Order("n_high:Q", sort="descending"),
    opacity=alt.condition(pick, alt.value(1), alt.value(0.3)),
    tooltip=["country:N", alt.Tooltip("high_label:N", title="High measures"), "count():Q"]
).add_params(pick).properties(width=260, height=520, title="Share of each country's regions")
(mapc.add_params(pick) | bars).configure_view(stroke=None)
```

## The three measures side by side

Each map shows one measure for the same regions. **Hover over a region** in any map and it lights up in all three, so you can compare the same place across measures.

```{python}
hover = alt.selection_point(fields=["region_id"], on="pointerover", clear="pointerout", empty=False)
def small(col, title):
    lab, scheme, dom = VAR[col]
    return alt.Chart(rg).mark_geoshape().encode(
        color=alt.Color(f"{col}:Q", scale=alt.Scale(scheme=scheme, domain=dom, clamp=True),
                        legend=alt.Legend(orient="bottom", title=lab, gradientLength=180)),
        stroke=alt.condition(hover, alt.value("black"), alt.value("white")),
        strokeWidth=alt.condition(hover, alt.value(2), alt.value(0.3)),
        tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("region:N", title="Region"), "country:N",
                 alt.Tooltip(f"{col}:Q", title=lab, format=".1f")]
    ).add_params(hover).project("equalEarth").properties(width=300, height=320, title=title)
alt.hconcat(small("anemia_pct", "Anemia"), small("od_pct", "Open defecation"),
            small("pfpr", "Malaria")).resolve_scale(color="independent").configure_view(stroke=None)
```

## Brush the scatterplot to filter everything

Each dot is a hexagon (about 3–10 DHS clusters), placed by how common open defecation is (x-axis) and how many children are anemic (y-axis), and coloured by malaria.

::: {.howto}
**Drag a box** on the scatterplot. The country bars and the malaria histogram update to show only the hexagons you selected. Use the **country menu** to highlight one country.
:::

```{python}
brush = alt.selection_interval(encodings=["x", "y"])
countries = sorted(hx.country.unique())
csel = alt.selection_point(fields=["country"], bind=alt.binding_select(options=[None] + countries,
                           labels=["All countries"] + countries, name="Highlight country: "))
scatter = alt.Chart(hx).mark_circle(stroke="white", strokeWidth=0.3).encode(
    x=alt.X("od_pct:Q", title="Households with no toilet (%)"),
    y=alt.Y("anemia_pct:Q", title="Children anemic (%)", scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, 100])),
    color=alt.condition(brush & csel, alt.Color("pfpr:Q", scale=alt.Scale(scheme="purples", domain=[0, 70]),
                        title="Malaria (%)"), alt.value("#e2e2e2")),
    size=alt.Size("n_clusters:Q", title="DHS clusters", scale=alt.Scale(range=[15, 220])),
    opacity=alt.condition(csel, alt.value(0.9), alt.value(0.25)),
    tooltip=["country:N", alt.Tooltip("anemia_pct:Q", format=".0f", title="Anemia %"),
             alt.Tooltip("od_pct:Q", format=".0f", title="No toilet %"),
             alt.Tooltip("pfpr:Q", format=".0f", title="Malaria %"), "n_clusters:Q"]
).add_params(brush, csel).properties(width=470, height=380)

cbar = alt.Chart(hx).mark_bar(color="#7b2d26").encode(
    y=alt.Y("country:N", sort="-x", title=None), x=alt.X("count():Q", title="Hexagons selected")
).transform_filter(brush).properties(width=200, height=380)

hist = alt.Chart(hx).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("pfpr:Q", bin=alt.Bin(maxbins=25), title="Malaria prevalence (%)"),
    y=alt.Y("count():Q", title="Hexagons"),
    color=alt.value("#756bb1")
).transform_filter(brush).properties(width=700, height=140, title="Malaria in the selected hexagons")

alt.vconcat(alt.hconcat(scatter, cbar), hist).configure_view(stroke=None)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
r = hx[["anemia_pct", "od_pct", "pfpr"]].corr().round(2)
print(f"""Across hexagons, anemia goes with malaria (correlation **{r.loc['anemia_pct','pfpr']}**) more than with open defecation (**{r.loc['anemia_pct','od_pct']}**). Open defecation and malaria are themselves only weakly related (**{r.loc['od_pct','pfpr']}**), so places with both are a distinct group, not the norm. The [profiles page](profiles.qmd) picks up from here.""")
```
